what_this_proves: The device reads pictures and archives as kinds of their own: an image's headers from WPF's decoder without decoding pixels, its text through the local Windows OCR engine (the owner's installed language packs, Turkish first, a typed refusal when none), a zip's central directory without inflating an entry. The cloud finds documents by the words in their text (from the index, no crawl), proposes duplicates by sha256 after locating each hit, sends exactly the proposal the owner heard to the Recycle Bin through a new reversible device capability, previews any document in its own units, speaks a picture's text and an archive's contents, and the executive compare finally honours its planner's two targets.

measured_first.device_before: FileKinds knew docx/xlsx/pptx/pdf/md/csv/json/source/txt/unknown; .png/.zip were 'unknown' (inspect fell to a text-decode, extract refused unknown_kind); no OCR/EXIF/zip listing anywhere; DocumentCapabilityNames.All=7; the companion TFM net10.0-windows carries no WinRT projection.
measured_first.ocr_engine_probe: Windows.Media.Ocr on this machine: languages en-US, tr; a generated 600x120 PNG 'Merhaba Dünya 1234' recognised exactly in 15 ms through PowerShell 5.1 WinRT (measured before any code was written).
measured_first.cloud_before: no full-text search over document_index (only the file-name search and the within-one-document token overlap); no duplicate/preview code; file.search records carry no sha256 (file.locate does); _kind_documents_compare ignored the planner's targets; 'Bu iki dokümanı karşılaştır' resolved to none ('doküman' unknown); 'Görseldeki metni oku' resolved to ui_read.

found_on_the_way.console_codepage: The PowerShell OCR host answered 'Merhaba D�nya 1234' - the child wrote in the console code page while the parent read UTF-8; [Console]::OutputEncoding is forced to UTF-8 in the script.
found_on_the_way.csharp_pattern: `kind is not Unknown and kind is not Archive` parses `and` as a pattern combinator (CS9135); `kind is not (Unknown or Archive)` is the form.
found_on_the_way.oracle_contains_shape: the oracle's 'contains' match reads a `contains` array per block, not `text`; the PNG expected extract carries both.
found_on_the_way.fetch_position: FileFetchTests pinned file.fetch as the LAST documents name; file.trash is appended after it and the test now pins both positions.
found_on_the_way.clarifying_registry: a tool that answers needs_clarification must be in its family's *_CLARIFYING_TOOLS (DOCUMENT_TOOL_NAMES) or the relay records a success - two tests went red until the four names were listed.
found_on_the_way.duplicate_fixture_glob: the fake file.search treated '*' as a word; it now honours a glob like the device.

M2 full text scores no query words -> 1 failure.
M3 dedup acts without a proposal -> 1 failure.
M4 a trash the device did not verify counts as done -> 1 failure.
M5 every file becomes a duplicate group -> 1 failure.

M6 (C#) file.inspect no longer lists an archive's directory -> 1 failure in the lab test (the first C# mutation, letting IsExtractable admit archives, stayed green because the extractor lookup refuses anyway - two guards, one behaviour; replaced).

runtime_proof.status: PROVEN_REAL (test lab, this desktop): Windows OCR read the committed fixture exactly ('Merhaba Dünya 1234', language tr), the archive fixture listed its two entries and refused extraction, a lab file went to the Recycle Bin and was gone from its folder; the production 'üretimde bir görselden metin çıkarıldı' is Karar 0's (READY_FOR_OWNER)
